lesson_title: Independent application A: limitations and future directions

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 4 of "Capstone Defense, Portfolio Completion, and Transition" (unit 6, grade 12) is an independent application on limitations and future directions. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 60–90 minutes. The unit is working toward: Defend the completed capstone portfolio in a chosen private or public mode, with a final statement, a critical response, and a transition plan. Today's work contributes to that by handling limitations and future directions at the independent application a stage, against the unit's wider topics of evidence assembly and portfolio completion, artist statement final revision, defense in a chosen private or public mode, and limitations and future directions. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Independently make one short original piece built around limitations and future directions, aiming at an effect you choose in advance. Write the intended effect first, in one sentence, before you begin. Make the piece, then step back and judge honestly whether the effect landed, citing the specific element that carries it and one element that works against it. Revise that second element and keep both versions. The work must be your own; a tutor may demonstrate technique or give feedback but must not make any part of the graded piece. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about limitations and future directions, and it belongs to "Capstone Defense, Portfolio Completion, and Transition", which also covers separate topics such as evidence assembly and portfolio completion. Close out with this check before you stop: State your result for limitations and future directions and the single strongest piece of evidence supporting it. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

Address the lesson objective: Apply limitations and future directions independently to an unfamiliar case.

Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: One original short piece, a pre-written intent statement, a two-element self-critique, and a revision with both versions kept.
critique_criteria: The intended effect was written in one sentence before work began.
The finished piece is original and uses the lesson's focus to pursue that effect.
The self-critique cites one element that carries the intent and one that works against it.
A revision of the weaker element exists and both versions are kept.
The graded piece is the student's own authorship; assistance did not make any part of it.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting limitations and future directions.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for limitations and future directions follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for limitations and future directions, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to limitations and future directions works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of limitations and future directions, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking limitations and future directions mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply limitations and future directions under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on limitations and future directions rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
